description: Public, human-reviewable paraphrases of supported rule scenarios. Executable authority remains in engine code and tests.

rules.plainLanguage: Deterministic agents move, fight, and complete a match.
Setup shuffles two decks, deals split hidden hands, and places Avatars.
The manifest accepts only exact deck-scoped supported card facts.
One mulligan returns at most three chosen cards to their deck bottoms and redraws.
First player skips its draw, establishes a domain, then second player chooses a deck.
Sites expand through unoccupied orthogonal cells controlled by their player.
A player with no sites recovers at the closest available cell.
The Avatar may draw a private site instead of playing one.
A draw-spell Avatar pays its tap cost and keeps the drawn identity private.
Drawing a site from an empty Atlas pays the tap cost and loses.
Forged spatial actions cannot mutate the game.
Sinkhole sacrifices sites into neutral Rubble and preserves relative subsurface.
A Spellcaster pays mana and summons a minion atop a controlled site.
Token Magic summons deterministically and tokens banish instead of entering a cemetery.
Aramos Mercenaries may discard a deterministic random hand card instead of paying mana.
Gnarled Wendigo sacrifices local minions before paying its discounted summon.
Hamlet reduces only Ordinary minion mana payments at that site.
Printed Spellcasters cast while tapped or summoning sick from their own location.
Targeted Magic is a non-unit source and resolves damage, Deathrite, and cemetery entry.
Duel makes a chosen ally fight a targeted enemy at the ally's location or a bordering location in the same region.
Leap Attack optionally steps an ally before it strikes every enemy there.
Leap Attack resumes its strike after ordered movement Deathrites.
Magic targets stay in the caster region and exclude enemy Stealth.
Lash damages then untaps only a surviving nearby minion target.
Freeze disables a nearby minion until the caster next Start Phase.
Disabling a subsurface minion immediately settles its region.
Lightning Bolt targets a location and deterministically damages one random unit there.
Lucky Charm commits the random action before exposing two deterministic outcomes.
Minor Explosion damages every unit at a location up to two cardinal steps away.
Chain Magic stages distinct nearby hops and damages all chosen units simultaneously.
Rain of Arrows simultaneously damages every aboveground minion.
Charge Magic grants an untargeted ally Charge only for the current turn.
Overpower changes current power for source-aware prevention until the current End Phase.
Nearby-allies power is derived and settles deaths when its source dies.
Controlled Mortal power follows current control and settles deaths.
Aura-loss Deathrite ends the game after its triggering Magic resolves.
Aura-loss deaths cannot restore stale combat during a defender path.
Lure makes a chosen enemy minion take its own closer step.
Teleport forcefully moves a chosen ally to a target site surface.
Blink teleports a nearby ally before deaths and a private chosen-deck draw.
Rescue returns a chosen own cemetery minion to hidden hand or resolves with none.
Bury forcefully burrows minions if able and immediately resolves survival.
Bury detaches and burrows Artifacts if able.
Cave-In burrows every eligible surface minion at one Land Site together.
Drown forcefully submerges a target minion if able.
Healing Magic is targetless, capped, and cannot leave Death's Door.
Explicit permission allows a minion to be summoned to any site.
A Water-site cast restriction filters unrestricted summons by terrain.
Waterbound derives Disabled from terrain and survives only with active abilities.
Region settlement kills inhospitable minions and banishes them from the void.
Playing a site surfaces uncarried Artifacts from the covered void.
Charge allows a summoned minion to Move and Attack immediately.
Genesis draws a hidden site and an empty Atlas loses after summoning.
Genesis draws a hidden spell and an empty Spellbook loses after summoning.
Numeric Genesis spell draw counts draw ordered hidden cards.
Numeric Genesis spell draws exhaust 2, 1, or 0 remaining cards before deck loss.

Genesis strike-each-enemy-here hits every enemy sharing the newcomer's cell, including the Avatar standing on its own site. Co-located allies and the striker are skipped. Ward absorbs a strike without dealing damage.
Vile Imp may deal 2 damage to one adjacent unit or decline.
Genesis life loss reaches but cannot cross Death's Door.
Grain Sparrow Genesis gains controller life through shared healing semantics.
Site Genesis grants temporary mana once, pays a summon, and expires.
Site Genesis heals every nearby Avatar through shared life caps.
Site Genesis makes units at nearby sites Immobile until its controller next turn.
Aura occupies any canonical 2x2 area and grounds site minions for three controller turns.
An end-turn Aura damages a random affected unit before its optional step.
Oversized minions occupy one canonical 2x2 footprint for movement, combat, Auras, and terrain.
Tower Genesis grants mana only for the first controlled copy.
Humble Village Genesis may spend its mana to summon one Foot Soldier.
Geomancer creates Rubble and privately replaces it with the top Atlas site.
Site Genesis resumes after ordered terrain-replacement Deathrites.
Hunter's Lodge Genesis removes only enemy Stealth.
Seasonal River Genesis privately keeps or bottoms the next spell.
Observatory privately reorders the next three spells without drawing.
Adjacent matching sites trigger one spell draw apiece and a short deck loses.
Site Genesis discards up to two top spells publicly without deck-out.
Vikings area damage uses bearer Lethal without becoming a strike.
A minion mana ability requires readiness, taps, and expires at End Phase.
Mana and every elemental threshold gate minion actions without being spent together.
An undamaged 0/0 Genesis minion survives until it takes positive damage.
An active minion prevents damage from a unit at its current-power threshold.
Ranged damage retains its attacking unit source classification.
A ready minion may tap to shoot a fixed-damage projectile to the first visible unit.
A restricted attacker can target units but not sites.
Attacking-only first strike resolves deaths before normal strikes and is inactive while defending.
Genesis sleep ends on real damage without retroactive strikes.
Lance buffs and breaks on the next unit strike but not a site strike.
Ranged strikes without return damage and Ward prevents the first positive damage event.
A surviving enabled minion may take one legal step after its Ranged strike.
An empty Ranged projectile does not offer the post-strike step.
A Ranged striker that dies during the hit cannot leave a pending step.
A Ranged unit may strike once during Move and Attack or Defend.
A drag projectile stops at the first visible unit and may fight after arrival.
A drag projectile resumes after ordered movement Deathrites before fighting.
Granary Rats suppresses its site threshold while enabled.
A provider adds affinity until that minion dies.
Lethal kills a tougher minion with positive damage but not zero damage.
A prohibited minion cannot move to Defend but can still Intercept.
Immobile units attack and Defend in place but cannot move themselves.
A fully prohibited minion cannot use Defend or Intercept.
Airborne moves diagonally and restricts attacks and Intercept.
Cloud City flies once per turn at three Air affinity and carries normal occupants.
Updraft Ridge gives only Airborne minions a free departure to move or Defend.
Mountain Pass blocks only occupied ground-minion entry.
Stealth blocks attacks, Defend, Intercept, and projectiles until interaction.
Sly Fox gains Stealth once at the end of its controller turn.
Conditional end-turn Stealth requires no nearby enemy in the same region.
Scent Hounds permanently removes nearby enemy Stealth.
Malakhim untaps at its controller End Phase unless Disabled.
Ignited dies before turn cleanup unless it is Disabled.
Sedge Crabs can move themselves only sideways.
Dalcean Phalanx can move itself only forward for its seat.
A unit can move across connected top and bottom realm edges.
Submerge uses underwater summons, movement, and region-isolated combat.
Burrowing uses underground summons and movement only at land sites.
Secret Tunnel connects burrowed allies only to the controller's other sites.
A must-be-burrowed cast restriction suppresses only non-underground casts.
A must-be-submerged cast restriction suppresses only non-underwater casts.
Combined region abilities permit eligible cross-region adjacency steps.
Voidwalk summons to any void and moves between adjacent void and surface locations.
Planar Gate grants minions Voidwalk only until they leave the void.
An outer-column cast restriction filters surface and Voidwalk summons, not movement.
Movement +1 issues exact two-step and returning Move and Attack paths.
Movement +1 can take an exact two-step path to Defend.
Movement +2 issues exact three-step paths and attacks after moving.
AP commits before NAP, then NAP Deathrites resolve before AP Deathrites.
NAP then AP Deathrites resolve before simultaneous deaths enter their cemeteries.
Bladderblimp Deathrite makes each player lose life for their nearby sites.
Deathrite damages each other remaining unit here in simultaneous chained batches.
Deathrite uses its moved last location with Ward, reduction, and Lethal.
Deathrite preserves its unit-source power snapshot before cemetery entry.
Deathrite healing caps at maximum, fails at Death's Door, and precedes cemetery entry.
Move and Attack stages movement before an undefended enemy-site strike.
Defend moves a unit into a simultaneous fight and stages exact split damage.
Takes-less prevention applies to each simultaneous damage source before Lethal.
Declining an attack gives only co-located ready enemies an Intercept window.
Surviving minion damage persists through the turn and clears in End Phase.
Death's Door prevents same-turn direct damage and later simultaneous death blows draw.
Later undefended site strikes cannot deliver Death's Door death blows.
Attempting to draw from an empty deck immediately loses.
Pick Up and Drop manage local carried Artifacts once per unit turn.
Dropping a power Artifact immediately kills a lethally wounded bearer.
A carried Lethal Artifact kills on positive strike damage and drops with its bearer.
Siege Ballista taps its bearer and another ally for measured artifact damage.
Payload Trebuchet discards a card for measured location damage.
Rolling Boulder rolls maximally and damages other units along its path.
Mesmerism transfers a minion and its Deathrite to the new controller.
Fatality kills only a wounded minion in the caster region.
Sparkmage may tap for zero damage at a nearby location with no other unit.
Sparkmage counts every player-cast spell source, resets, and damages one other unit.
Sparkmage chooses among multiple other units with deterministic private RNG.
An active surface minion derives power, Ranged, and Spellcaster atop a Tower.
A minion discards a chosen Spellbook card to damage a random other unit here.
Random other-unit damage includes allied, enemy, Avatar, and Stealth candidates.
Discard damage snapshots derived unit power and uses Ward and prevention.
Artifacts make their current site controller lose life at each turn end.
End-turn Artifact life loss uses its carried cell and survives bearer Disable.
End-turn Artifact life loss respects regions, Rubble, stacking, and Death's Door.
Start-turn random teleports resolve in controller-chosen order through Lucky Charm.
Raise Dead selects a public random cemetery minion before free placement.
Craterize discards a site, destroys its target, and applies the printed damage grid.
Cave-In detaches or carries eligible Artifacts underground and merges their outcomes with minions in canonical identity order.
Geomancer Rubble replacement resumes the same adjacent same-card Spellbook draws as playing that site from hand.
Waterbound Disable suppresses printed abilities but the Ward mark still prevents the next damage.
Waterbound Disable skips end-turn Stealth and permanently reveals it; returning to Water can gain Stealth on a later End Phase.
Waterbound Genesis still draws after summoning onto Water.
A Waterbound Stealth token enters stealthed on Water.
An oversized minion's Genesis still draws after occupying a canonical 2x2.
A printed Spellcaster occupying a 2x2 originates Nearby Magic from every footprint cell.
An oversized Deathrite damages every other unit sharing any occupied footprint cell.
Oversized Genesis here damages every other unit sharing any occupied footprint cell.
An oversized Genesis strike hits enemies sharing any occupied footprint cell and skips allies.
Optional adjacent Genesis from a 2x2 reaches units orthogonally bordering any footprint cell.
Discard-funded random-here from a 2x2 damages a hidden other unit sharing any occupied footprint cell.
A 2x2 with summonToAnySite may occupy any canonical square whose every cell has surface terrain.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion stays enabled when any occupied cell is a Water site.
Threshold suppression from a 2x2 covers every occupied site, not only the anchor.
A 2x2 Ranged minion originates cardinal projectiles from every occupied footprint cell.
A 2x2 gains power, Ranged, and Spellcaster when any occupied cell is a Tower.
A 2x2 Ordinary minion pays Hamlet's destination discount when any occupied cell is that Site.
A 2x2 sacrifice discount selects controlled minions on every occupied summoning cell, not only the anchor.
A 2x2 water-site cast is illegal when any occupied cell is land, even if another occupied cell is Water.
A 2x2 water-site cast may occupy an enemy all-Water square when every occupied cell is Water.
A 2x2 activated projectile originates cardinal rays from every occupied footprint cell.
A 2x2 drag projectile originates from every occupied cell and hauls the hit unit back to that origin, not only the anchor.
A 2x2 Burrowing minion can be summoned underground only when every occupied cell is land.
A 2x2 Submerge minion can be summoned underwater only when every occupied cell is Water.
A 2x2 minion that must be cast burrowed is offered only the underground placement of an all-land square.
A 2x2 minion that must be cast submerged is offered only the underwater placement of an all-Water square.
A 2x2 area-damage minion can blanket a location adjacent to any occupied footprint cell and never targets its own square.
A 2x2 nearby-ally power aura reaches units nearby any occupied footprint cell, including a cell that is not nearby the anchor.
A 2x2 Scent Hounds effect permanently removes Stealth from enemies nearby any occupied footprint cell.
A 2x2 minion that gains Stealth only with no nearby enemies treats an enemy nearby any occupied footprint cell as nearby.
A 2x2 minion that gains Stealth only with no nearby enemies still gains it when the only enemy Avatar is far from every occupied cell.
A 2x2 minion that may Ranged strike once during basic movement can fire from any occupied footprint cell while the square is still on its starting cells.
A 2x2 minion that may step after a Ranged strike translates every occupied footprint cell when it takes that optional step.
Targetless draw-spell Magic pays its cost, draws the printed number of hidden Spellbook cards in deck order, and enters its owner's cemetery. The opponent sees only the new hand count.
Targetless draw-spell Magic draws every remaining Spellbook card it can, then loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library.

Unconditional kill-minion Magic pays its cost, offers every same-region minion including healthy copies, never offers an Avatar, and destroys the chosen minion through the shared kill and Deathrite pipeline.
Unconditional kill-minion Magic that would destroy a Warded minion breaks Ward instead, leaves the minion in play with no damage, and still resolves.
Targetless draw-site Magic pays its cost, draws the printed number of hidden Atlas cards in deck order, and enters its owner's cemetery. The opponent sees only the new Atlas hand count.
Targetless draw-site Magic draws every remaining Atlas card it can, then loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library.

Bounce Magic pays its cost, offers every same-region minion including healthy copies, never offers an Avatar, and returns the chosen minion to its owner's hidden Spellbook hand without dying or entering a cemetery. The opponent sees only the new hand count.
Bounce Magic that would return a Warded minion to hand breaks Ward instead, leaves the minion in play, and still resolves.
Defending first strike resolves the defender's strike, deaths, and Deathrites before the attacker can strike, so a lethal defender takes no return damage.
Defending-only first strike is inactive while attacking, so a defending-only first-strike attacker and a vanilla defender trade simultaneously.

Printed first strike is the combination of attacking and defending first strike: the same minion kills before a return strike while attacking and takes no damage from a simultaneous attacker while defending.

Destroy-site Magic pays its cost, offers every real site including the caster's own, never offers Rubble or a void, replaces the chosen site with Rubble, and moves that site into its owner's cemetery. Occupants remain on the Rubble.
Destroy-site Magic that would destroy a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site in play, and still resolves.

Return-site Magic pays its cost, offers every real site including the caster's own, never offers Rubble or a void, returns the chosen site to its owner's Atlas hand, leaves no Rubble, and banishes surface minions that occupied the site. Avatars remain at the emptied cell.
Return-site Magic that would return a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site and its occupants in play, and still resolves.

Destroy-artifact Magic pays its cost, offers every Artifact in the caster region whether loose or carried, moves a real Artifact into its owner's cemetery, and leaves no later Artifact target once the realm is empty of them.
Return-artifact Magic detaches a carried Artifact and returns it to its owner's Spellbook hand. The opponent sees only the resulting hand count, and the Artifact does not enter a cemetery.
Target-player life-loss Magic pays its cost, offers only both Avatars, never offers a minion, and reduces the chosen Avatar's life without dealing damage. The loss is not a death blow.
Target-player life-loss Magic that reduces an Avatar to zero life reaches Death's Door without ending the game. Further life loss against that Avatar is a no-op and is never a death blow.

Target-player life-gain Magic pays its cost, offers only both Avatars, never offers a minion, and heals the chosen Avatar through the shared printed-life cap. Unlike controller-only healing, it can restore an opponent.
Target-player life-gain Magic that would heal an Avatar at Death's Door is a paid no-op. Life stays at zero, the game stays active, and no healing event is emitted.
Untap-minion Magic pays its cost, offers only same-region minions, never offers an Avatar, and readies a tapped minion without dealing damage or breaking Ward.
Untap-minion Magic that targets an already-untapped minion is a paid no-op. The minion stays ready, keeps Ward, and no untap event is emitted.
Tap-minion Magic pays its cost, offers only same-region minions, never offers an Avatar, and marks a ready minion tapped. A second cast on the already-tapped minion is a paid no-op.
Tap-minion Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks, the minion stays ready, and no tap event is emitted.
Grant-Ward Magic pays its cost, offers only same-region minions, never offers an Avatar, and marks an unwarded minion with Ward without dealing damage or breaking an existing mark.
Grant-Ward Magic that targets an already-warded minion is a paid no-op. The minion keeps Ward and no grant event is emitted.
Grant-Stealth Magic pays its cost, offers only same-region visible minions, never offers an Avatar, and marks an enemy minion Stealthed. After the grant, that enemy is no longer a legal target.
Grant-Stealth Magic does not offer an already-stealthed enemy minion. The spell cannot be cast when that is the only candidate, and the printed Stealth mark stays.

Mill-spell Magic offers only both Avatars, never a minion, and puts the printed number of the chosen player's top Spellbook cards into that owner's cemetery in deck order. Identities are public. The game stays active when cards remain.
Mill-spell Magic that finds an empty Spellbook is a paid no-op. It does not draw, does not lose to deck-out, and emits no discard events.
Mill-site Magic is the Atlas sibling of mill-spell Magic: it offers only both Avatars and puts top Atlas cards into the owner's cemetery in deck order without drawing or decking.
Mill-site Magic that finds an empty Atlas is a paid no-op. It does not draw, does not lose to deck-out, and emits no discard events.

Cemetery Magic return is the Rescue sibling for Magic cards: it offers only Magic in the caster's own cemetery, never a minion, site, artifact, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.
Cemetery Magic return that finds no Magic in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Artifact return is the Rescue sibling for Artifacts: it offers only Artifacts in the caster's own cemetery, never a Magic card, minion, site, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.

Cemetery Artifact return that finds no Artifact in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Site return is the Rescue sibling for Sites: it offers only Sites in the caster's own cemetery, never Magic already there, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Atlas hand rather than the Spellbook.

Cemetery Site return that finds no Site in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

A player-chosen additional discard cost is a Storyline choice among every other hand card. It cannot select the spell being cast, pays into the owner's cemetery before the cast is announced, and then the companion effect resolves.
The same additional discard cost may take an Atlas card instead of a spell. Every issued cast includes the chosen identity; there is no no-choice cast while another hand card remains.

A start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw is a start-turn trigger. It draws the printed number of hidden spells through the shared private-draw helper before the Draw step, redacts those identities from the opponent, and leaves the ordinary Draw step pending.
The same start-turn Spellbook draw loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library. That required empty draw is a deck-out, not a paid no-op, and the Draw step never begins.

Target-player discard Magic offers only both Avatars. After the cast is announced, the targeted player chooses one of their own Atlas or Spellbook hand cards. The choice is a pending Storyline that transfers the decision seat; the caster cannot pick the card, and opponent hand identities stay redacted until the discard is public in the cemetery.
The same targeted discard is a paid no-op when the chosen player has no hand cards. It never becomes a random discard and never decks out.

A start-of-controller-turn Atlas draw is a start-turn trigger. It draws the printed number of hidden sites through the shared private-draw helper before the Draw step, redacts those identities from the opponent, and leaves the ordinary Draw step pending.
The same start-turn Atlas draw loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library. That required empty draw is a deck-out, not a paid no-op, and the Draw step never begins.

A minion that must attack a unit if able treats that attack as a mandatory main-phase action. While a legal unit attack is in its range of motion, the engine offers only those Move and Attack paths and then requires a unit Declare Attack. Optional main-phase actions and Decline Attack wait.
The same mandatory-attack fact does not constrain the main phase when no enemy unit is in range of motion. Ordinary optional actions, including End Turn, remain legal.

A minion that enemies must attack if able forces every opposing minion that can reach it. Those minions may take only Move and Attack paths that can strike it, then must Declare Attack on it. Optional main-phase actions and Decline Attack wait.
The same forced-attack source does not constrain an opposing minion that cannot reach it. Ordinary optional actions, including End Turn, remain legal.

An artifact that nearby minions must attack if able forces every nearby opposing minion that can attack. Those minions may take only Move and Attack actions, then must Declare Attack while they remain nearby and have a target. Optional main-phase actions and Decline Attack wait.
The same nearby-must-attack artifact does not constrain a minion that is not nearby. Ordinary optional actions, including End Turn, remain legal.
A minion forced by a nearby-must-attack artifact may choose a Move and Attack path that leaves nearby. After it is no longer nearby, Declare Attack is optional and Decline Attack is legal.
Nearby strikes against units deal double damage. The multiplier uses the struck unit's location, composes with nearby-must-attack on the same Artifact, and stacks by doubling once per nearby source.
The same nearby-double-strike fact does not change a strike whose struck unit is not nearby the source. A 1-power undoubled strike leaves a 2-defense minion wounded.
A Ranged strike deals double damage when the struck unit is nearby a nearby-double-strike source. The multiplier uses the struck unit's location, not the shooter's.
The same nearby-double-strike fact does not change a Ranged strike whose struck unit is not nearby the source. A 1-power undoubled projectile leaves a 2-defense minion wounded.
A Genesis strike deals double damage when the struck unit is nearby a nearby-double-strike source. The multiplier uses the struck unit's location.
The same nearby-double-strike fact does not change a Genesis strike whose struck unit is not nearby the source. A 1-power undoubled Genesis strike leaves a 2-defense minion wounded.
A start-of-controller-turn lure forces a nearby same-region enemy minion to take one card-effect step toward the source. The ability is mandatory, does not tap, and cannot be intercepted.
The same start-of-controller-turn lure is a paid no-op when no nearby same-region enemy minion exists. The Start Phase then continues to the Draw step.
A start-of-controller-turn Aura on an Ordinary or Exceptional site destroys that site, the minions standing atop it, and itself. Avatars are not minions and survive on the resulting rubble.
The same start-of-controller-turn Aura still destroys an empty Ordinary site and itself, without killing the Avatar. Unique or Legendary sites are not legal conjure targets.

A start-of-controller-turn life-loss ability makes the controller lose the printed amount of life, then the Start Phase continues to the Draw step. The ability is mandatory and does not tap the source.
The same start-of-controller-turn life loss can reduce the controller to 0 life and open Death's Door without immediately ending the game. The Start Phase still continues to the Draw step.

A wandering end-of-each-turn Aura conjures atop a single nearby site, deals its printed damage to each unit there, then must move to an adjacent location it has not visited. The move is mandatory and does not hold or immobilize the area.
The same wandering Aura cannot be conjured on a site that is not nearby the spellcaster. It triggers at the end of each player's turn, and it dispels when no unvisited adjacent location remains.

An Artifact can grant its current site a start-of-controller-turn ability that makes that player lose the printed life and gain the same amount of mana this turn. The Artifact remains, and the Start Phase continues to the Draw step.

The same site-granted start-of-turn life loss can reduce the site controller to 0 life and open Death's Door without immediately ending the game. The printed mana gain still happens, and the Start Phase still continues to the Draw step.

A persistent 2×2 Aura can flood affected sites. Those sites become Water sites and still provide their other elemental affinities. The Aura does not immobilize, does not use the 3-turn duration machine, and remains after the controller's next turn starts.

A later-entered persistent 2×2 Drought Aura covering the same site wins the timestamp: the site is no longer a Water site and provides no Water threshold, while its other affinities remain. Flood entered first stays in the realm.

A minion can gain its controller a printed amount of life at the start of that player's turn. The heal uses the shared Avatar helper, is capped at printed life, and the Start Phase continues to the Draw step.

The same start-of-controller-turn life gain cannot take an Avatar off Death's Door. The trigger still resolves, the minion remains, and the Start Phase continues to the Draw step with the game active.

Magic can destroy a realm Aura. The Aura moves to its owner's cemetery, matching immobile areas lift, Flood or Drought water overlays leave the covered sites, and the event is aura-destroyed rather than a duration dispel.
Magic can return a realm Aura to its owner's Spellbook hand. The Aura leaves the realm, Flood water leaves the covered sites, and the opponent sees only the updated hand count.

Magic can return an Aura from its caster's own cemetery to the hidden Spellbook hand. Only Aura cards are offered, so a destroy Magic already in that cemetery is not a legal choice, and the opponent sees only the updated hand count.

The same cemetery Aura return still pays and resolves when the caster's cemetery has no Aura. The spell enters the cemetery, no Aura returns, and a later Magic card there is not offered as a substitute target.

Magic can grant Airborne to a controlled ally for the current turn. The grant is recorded on minions as a temporary source, public observations show the minion as Airborne, and the shared End Phase cleanup expires the source.
A grounded minion cannot strike an Airborne enemy. After grant-Airborne Magic, the same minion can declare that strike. The opponent still sees only the updated Spellbook hand count.

Magic can grant Ranged to a controlled ally for the current turn. After summoning sickness clears, the minion may shoot a projectile. The grant is recorded as a temporary source and the shared End Phase cleanup expires it.

Granted Ranged does not bypass summoning sickness. Charge lets a sick minion Move and Attack; it does not let that minion shoot, and grant-Ranged Magic does not either. The opponent sees only the updated Spellbook hand count.
Magic can grant Lethal to a controlled ally for the current turn. The grant is recorded as a temporary source and the shared End Phase cleanup expires it.
A 1-power minion without Lethal only wounds a 2-defense enemy. After grant-Lethal Magic, the same strike destroys that enemy. The opponent still sees only the updated Spellbook hand count.

At the start of its controller's turn, a minion can deal damage to each other unit sharing its footprint. The pulse reaches both seats, including a Surface Avatar on the same cell, and does not hit the source.

Start-of-turn here-area damage is lethal enough to destroy a 1-defense visitor sharing the cell. The source remains, the controller Avatar still takes the pulse, and the visitor enters its owner's cemetery.
Magic can grant First Strike to a controlled ally for the current turn. The grant is recorded as a temporary source and the shared End Phase cleanup expires it.

Equal 3/3 combat without First Strike is simultaneous. After grant-First-Strike Magic, the same attacker kills before taking return damage. The opponent still sees only the updated Spellbook hand count.
At the start of its controller's turn, a minion can add mana to the site-produced pool already present in the Start Phase. The trigger is mandatory and then the turn proceeds to Draw.
Start-of-turn controller mana gain can pay a two-mana spell that one site alone cannot. After Draw, the gained mana is spent and the pool returns to empty.
Target-player Spellbook draw Magic makes the chosen player draw from that player's remaining Spellbook. Drawn card identities stay private, including in events and the opponent's public view.
Target-player Spellbook draw on an empty library is a deck-out for the targeted player, not a paid no-op. That is the opposite of mill, which leaves the game active when the library is empty.
Target-player Atlas draw Magic makes the chosen player draw from that player's remaining Atlas. Drawn site identities stay private, including in events and the opponent's public view.
Target-player Atlas draw on an empty library is a deck-out for the targeted player, not a paid no-op. That is the opposite of mill, which leaves the game active when the Atlas is empty.

At the end of its controller's turn, a minion can deal damage to each other unit sharing its footprint. The pulse hits both seats, including a Surface Avatar on the same cell, and never hits the source. End Phase then removes leftover damage from survivors before the opponent draws.

End-of-controller-turn here-area damage can destroy a 1-defense visitor on the same cell. The source remains, Deathrites resolve through the existing end-turn continuation, and the opponent then draws.

At the start of its controller's turn, a minion can mill the top Spellbook card into that player's cemetery. The discarded identity is public, the hand is unchanged, and the Start Phase then proceeds to Draw.

A start-of-controller-turn Spellbook mill is a no-op when the library is empty. The game stays active, no card is discarded, and the Start Phase still proceeds to Draw. Required start-turn draws still deck out.
At the start of its controller's turn, a minion can mill the top Atlas card into that player's cemetery. The discarded site identity is public and the Start Phase then proceeds to Draw.
A start-of-controller-turn Atlas mill is a no-op when the Atlas is empty. The game stays active and the Start Phase still proceeds to Draw.
When a minion dies, Deathrite can draw a hidden Spellbook card for its controller before the corpse enters the cemetery. The opponent sees only the hand count.
A Deathrite Spellbook draw from an empty library is a deck-out. The corpse still dies, the game ends, and no card is drawn. Deathrite site draws keep the same empty-library loss.
Heal-target-minion Magic removes damage from a living minion in the same turn it was wounded. Avatars are not legal targets. The heal does not kill the minion.
Healing an undamaged minion is a paid no-op. No heal event is emitted, Ward is not broken, and the minion stays in play at zero damage.
When a minion dies, Deathrite can mill the top Spellbook card into the cemetery before the corpse enters. The milled identity is public. An empty Spellbook does not lose.
A Deathrite Spellbook mill from an empty library is a no-op. The corpse still dies, the game stays active, and no card is discarded.
When a minion dies, Deathrite can mill the top Atlas card into the cemetery before the corpse enters. The milled identity is public.
A Deathrite Atlas mill from an empty library is a no-op. The corpse still dies and the game stays active.
A minion can gain its controller a printed amount of life at the end of that player's turn. The heal uses the shared Avatar helper and is capped at printed life.
The same end-of-controller-turn life gain cannot take an Avatar off Death's Door. The pulse still runs, the minion remains, and the game stays active.
A minion can make its controller lose a printed amount of life at the end of that player's turn. The ability is mandatory and does not tap the source.
The same end-of-controller-turn life loss can reduce the controller to 0 life and open Death's Door without immediately ending the game.
A minion can skip the controller Start Phase untap. After it taps, it stays tapped on that player's next turn and cannot Move and Attack until something else readies it.
Disable suppresses the Start Phase doesn't-untap replacement. A frozen copy untaps with the rest of the controller's minions, then Freeze expires at the caster's next turn start.
A 2×2 Aura can flood only non-Ordinary sites. Those sites become Water sites and provide only Water threshold. Ordinary sites under the same area keep their printed elements and are not flooded.
The same Aura's Genesis submerges minions atop affected non-Ordinary sites. A minion without Submerge dies through region settlement and enters its owner's cemetery.
A Monument Artifact can untap all nearby allies at the end of its conjurer's turn. Nearby includes the Artifact's own square. Allies include the conjurer's Avatar and minions.
The same Monument does not emit nearby-ally untap events at the end of the opponent's turn. A nearby ally can tap to Defend during that turn; Start Phase may later ready it silently.
A Monument Artifact can be conjured onto a controlled site but cannot be conjured onto a unit and cannot be picked up.
An ordinary Artifact sharing the Monument's square can still be picked up. The Monument stays out of every Pick Up combination.
A 2x2 Voidwalk minion can be summoned only onto an all-void square. A mixed surface/void square and a covered site are not void destinations.
A 2x2 Voidwalk minion can step from one all-void square to another. Existing whole-footprint and one-step helpers do not offer a step onto surface, because those squares overlap.
A Landbound minion is enabled on a land site and becomes Disabled when it occupies no land location. The minion stays in the realm. Mixed Water sites are not land.
Flood makes the occupied site a Water site, so a Landbound minion becomes Disabled in place. The Landbound ability itself still applies while Disabled.
A Magic card with a printed Pay Life additional cost spends that life before the cast is announced. Paying life is not losing life or damage. The spell then resolves.
Pay Life is legal only when current life is at least the printed amount. Paying the remaining life reaches Death's Door without a death blow. Death's Door cannot pay any life.
Drought makes the occupied Water site a land location, so a Landbound minion becomes enabled in place. The minion stays in the realm.
A site can prevent units whose power is at least a printed threshold from entering. A minion at or above that power cannot be summoned onto the site or step onto it. A weaker minion still can.
Site entry uses current derived power. A later power grant can close an otherwise legal step onto a threshold site without changing the minion's printed attack.

A 2x2 minion cannot be summoned onto a square that includes a power-threshold site it is too strong to enter. Another legal 1x1 cell in the same square does not make the occupancy legal. A weaker 2x2 still can occupy that square.
A 2x2 minion cannot take a step that newly occupies a power-threshold site it is too strong to enter. Already occupied cells of the footprint do not waive the check on newly entered cells.

Fate is a Lose effect. A covered non-Ordinary site loses its printed power-threshold bar, so a unit that was too strong to step onto that site can enter after Fate covers it. Fate Genesis still submerges occupants of affected sites, so the unit must start off the covered site.

Teleport and free placement use the same Fate-aware power-threshold helper as movement. Fate lifts the bar on a covered non-Ordinary site. An Ordinary site in the same 2x2 keeps its printed threshold.

Cemetery free placement uses the power the minion would have on that site, not printed attack. A printed-1 minion that would become 3 atop a Tower cannot Raise Dead onto a threshold-3 Tower. The same corpse can still land on an open site.

A 2x2 Raise Dead uses the power the minion would have on the whole footprint. A Tower on one cell of the square raises that power, so a threshold site on another cell of the same square blocks occupancy. An all-open square remains legal.
Tokens are units, so creating one on a site is an entry. A Genesis paid token whose printed power meets a site's power-threshold bar cannot be paid onto that site. A weaker token still can.

Genesis token placement uses the power the token would have on that site, not printed attack. A printed-1 token that would become 3 atop the Tower it is spawning on cannot be paid onto a threshold-3 Tower. The same token can still be paid onto a Tower without a bar.

Fate is a Lose effect. A covered non-Ordinary site loses its printed Genesis paid-token ability, so the engine does not offer Pay 1 to summon that token onto the covered cell. Decline remains legal. Fate can cover voids, so the site is played onto the covered cell without standing a minion there first.
An Ordinary site in a Fate 2x2 keeps its printed abilities. Its Genesis paid-token choice stays legal, and paying still summons the token onto that site.

Fate is a Lose effect. A covered non-Ordinary Tower loses its printed bonus, so a minion that would become 3 with Ranged and Spellcaster atop that Tower stays at printed power and gains neither ability. Fate can cover voids, so the Tower is played onto the covered cell without standing a minion there first.
An Ordinary Tower in a Fate 2x2 keeps its printed abilities. A minion atop it still becomes 3 and is credited with Ranged and Spellcaster.

Fate floods a covered non-Ordinary earth site the same way playing Water onto rubble floods the layer beneath it. A Burrowing and Submerge minion already underground there is relayered underwater and stays in play. Fate Genesis still only submerges surface occupants. Fate can cover voids, so this proof keeps C4 uncovered and never stands the Avatar on a flooded site.

Drought makes a printed Water site land again. A Burrowing and Submerge minion already underwater there is relayered underground and stays in play, the same conversion that destroying a current Water site uses.

Destroying Flood flips a covered earth site back to land. A Burrowing and Submerge minion Flood had relayered underwater is relayered underground and stays in play. Returning or dispelling that Aura uses the same conversion.

Destroying Drought restores a printed Water site. A Burrowing and Submerge minion Drought had relayered underground is relayered underwater and stays in play. Returning or dispelling that Aura uses the same conversion.

Site flight carries occupants to the destination cell. When a Flooded Air site flies onto a dry void, a Burrowing and Submerge minion Flood had relayered underwater is relayered underground and stays in play.
Flood can cover voids. When an Air site flies onto a covered empty cell, that cell becomes Water and a Burrowing and Submerge minion already underground is relayered underwater and stays in play.

Playing printed earth onto Flood-covered rubble makes that cell a Water site. A Burrowing and Submerge minion already underground there is relayered underwater and stays in play. Geomancer rubble replacement uses the same conversion.

Playing printed Water onto Drought-covered rubble makes that cell land. A Burrowing and Submerge minion the Water play flooded underwater is relayered underground and stays in play. Geomancer rubble replacement uses the same conversion.
Return-site Magic leaves no Rubble. A Burrowing minion underground on the returned site is remapped into the void and banished. It does not die as if stranded on missing terrain.
Return-site Magic leaves no Rubble. A Submerge minion underwater on the returned site is remapped into the void and banished. It does not die as if stranded on missing terrain.

Return-site Magic remaps every unit that occupies the returned cell, not only a unit whose anchor is that cell. A 2×2 surface minion anchored at B3 that occupies C3 is banished when C3 is returned. It does not die as if stranded on missing terrain.

Return-site Magic remaps a 2×2 underground occupant the same way. A Burrowing square anchored at B3 that occupies C3 is banished when C3 is returned. It does not die as if stranded on missing terrain.
Creating adjacent Rubble while playing an earth site fills that void. A Voidwalk minion already in that void surfaces on the Rubble and stays in play. It is not banished as if stranded.
Creating adjacent Rubble while playing an earth site fills that void. A loose Artifact already in that void surfaces on the Rubble, the same way playing a site surfaces the Artifacts its void held.
Flying a site onto a nearby void fills that void. A Voidwalk minion already in that void surfaces on the arrived site and stays in play. It is not banished as if stranded.

Flying a site onto a nearby void fills that void. A loose Artifact already in that void surfaces on the arrived site, the same way playing a site or creating rubble surfaces the Artifacts its void held.

Cave-In burrows every surface minion that occupies the target land site. A 2×2 square that occupies that cell and also covers Water is still hit. Occupancy then kills the illegal underground footprint. The minion does not stay on the surface unharmed.

Cave-In burrows a 2×2 that occupies the target land cell even when its anchor is another cell. An all-land Burrowing square anchored at B3 that occupies C4 goes underground and stays in play when C4 is Cave-In'd.

Fate Genesis submerges every surface minion that occupies an affected non-Ordinary site. A 2×2 square that occupies that cell and also covers land is still hit. Occupancy then kills the illegal underwater footprint. The minion does not stay on the surface unharmed.

Fate Genesis submerges a 2×2 that occupies an affected non-Ordinary site even when its anchor is another cell. An all-Water Submerge square anchored at B3 that occupies C3 stays underwater when Fate covers C3 and leaves C4 uncovered.

Secret Tunnel connects a burrowed 2×2 that occupies the controller's tunnel, even when the square's anchor is another cell. A B3-anchored underground square that occupies C4 hops to a far controlled land site. Occupancy, not the anchor cell, decides whether the square is at that tunnel.

A burrowed 2×2 that occupies no Secret Tunnel cannot hop to a far controlled land site. Ordinary underground steps still require adjacent land. The same B3-anchored square without a tunnel under it stays local.

Measured-range Magic walks from every cell a 2×2 Spellcaster occupies, not only the anchor. A B3-anchored square occupying C4 can Minor-Explosion D4, which is one cardinal step from C4 and three from B3.
Measured-range Magic still stops at two cardinal steps. A B3-anchored 2×2 Spellcaster cannot Minor-Explosion E3, because that site is three steps from every occupied cell.

Updraft Ridge frees the first departure of an Airborne minion that occupies the Ridge, not only one whose path anchor stands there. A B3-anchored 2×2 occupying a Ridge at C4 can take two surface steps to B1.
An Airborne 2×2 that occupies no Updraft Ridge cannot take two surface steps. Ordinary one-step departure from the same B3-anchored square remains legal.

Flood makes a printed earth site a current Water site for casting. A water-site-only minion can be summoned to that flooded earth, and a submerged-only minion can be summoned underwater there. Printed earth without Flood remains illegal for both casts.
Drought makes a printed Water site not a Water site for casting. A water-site-only minion can be summoned there before Drought and cannot after Drought covers it.
A 2×2 bearer that occupies a helper stands with that helper for a tap-pair Artifact. A B3-anchored square carrying a Siege Ballista remembered at C4 can tap a ready ally on B3 for the second cost.
A helper that shares no occupied cell with a 2×2 bearer cannot pay a tap-pair Artifact's second tap. An ally on B2 does not stand with a B3-anchored square occupying B3, B4, C3, and C4.

A tap-pair Artifact measures range from every cell its 2×2 bearer occupies. A B3-anchored square carrying a Siege Ballista remembered at B3 can shoot a unit on D4, which is three steps from B3 and one step from occupied C4.
A tap-pair Artifact cannot shoot a unit three measured steps from every occupied bearer cell. E3 is three steps from a B3-anchored square along existing surface and stays out of Siege Ballista range.

Lucky Charm extra-random for discard-funded damage uses every cell a 2×2 source occupies. A B3 occupant of an A3-anchored square is offered, and resolving that outcome deals the printed damage to that unit.

Lucky Charm extra-random for discard-funded damage does not offer a unit outside the source footprint. A minion on C1 stays out of an A3-anchored square's committed outcomes and takes no damage when the B3 occupant is chosen.
A 2×2 token created by Genesis paid entry occupies its whole footprint on the realm grid.
When a 2×2 token dies in combat it banishes instead of entering a cemetery.
A 2×2 minion with top/bottom wraparound can be summoned onto a wrapped footprint that spans rank 1 and rank 4 across two adjacent files.
A 2×2 minion with top/bottom wraparound translates its whole footprint when the anchor steps across the connected edge, from a canonical square to the wrapped occupancy.
A 2×2 minion with an outer-column cast restriction can be summoned legally when its anchor sits in column A or E and occupies the full canonical footprint.
An outer-column cast restriction on a 2×2 minion filters summons only; after it enters play the whole footprint may step into inner columns.

Two distinct synthetic 30/60 decks complete a short deterministic opening: both seats keep their mulligans, establish domains, and summon at least one minion each, with byte-identical authoritative replay.
A deck-pair batch job with distinct north and south deck identities reproduces the same transcript hash when rerun with the same manifest and seed, regardless of worker count.
Start-turn random teleports move a 2×2 Voidwalk minion's whole footprint to an all-void or all-surface square.
Start-turn random teleports for a 2×2 Voidwalk minion resolve blocked footprints through Lucky Charm without moving the unit.
A token minion with printed Genesis draws a hidden Atlas card when it enters the realm.
A token minion with disable-until-damaged Genesis enters Disabled when it is created.
A token minion with adjacent-damage Genesis offers decline and nearby target branches when it enters through paid site Genesis.
A token minion with adjacent-damage Genesis offers decline and nearby target branches when Magic summons it to a site bordering an enemy site.
A B3-anchored 2x2 Spellcaster begins Chain Magic using footprint nearby cells, not the Avatar cell alone.
An oversized Spellcaster extends Chain Magic from each staged hop's occupied cells and rejects distant targets.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw and mill, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw first, then mill the new top card. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.
In that stacked draw-then-mill trigger, the mill is a paid no-op once the draw leaves an empty Spellbook. The game continues to the Draw step instead of decking out.

When one minion carries both end-of-controller-turn Avatar life gain and life loss, the End Phase resolves them in order on that minion before here-area damage: gain first, then loss. Both pulses apply to the controller Avatar and net together.

When one minion carries both end-of-controller-turn Avatar life gain and here-area damage, the End Phase resolves life gain first, then here-area damage through the existing end-turn continuation path.

When one minion carries all three end-of-controller-turn pulses—Avatar life gain, Avatar life loss, and here-area damage—the End Phase resolves them in order on that minion: gain first, then loss on the controller Avatar, then here-area damage through the existing end-turn continuation path.

When a minion carrying all three end-of-controller-turn pulses is Disabled, none of those pulses fire at end of turn: life gain and loss are skipped in the controller-life resolver and here-area damage is omitted from the end-turn continuation path.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Atlas draw and Spellbook draw, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw a site first, then draw a spell. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Atlas draw and mill, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw the top site, then mill the new top site into the cemetery. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw and Avatar life gain, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw a spell first, then heal the controller. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw and Avatar life loss, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw a spell first, then reduce the controller's life. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw and controller mana gain, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw a spell first, then add mana to the site-produced pool. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Atlas draw and here-area damage, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single trigger: draw a site first, then allocate damage to each other unit sharing the footprint. Both effects share one resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Avatar life gain and life loss, the Start Phase resolves them in order on that minion before other exclusive pulses: gain first, then loss. Both pulses apply to the controller Avatar and net together on a single resolve-start-turn-trigger action.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Avatar life gain and here-area damage, the Start Phase resolves life gain first, then here-area damage through the existing start-turn continuation path on a single resolve-start-turn-trigger action.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw and random teleport, the Start Phase resolves the hidden Spellbook draw first, then the random teleport on a single resolve-start-turn-trigger action before the Draw step.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Atlas draw and random teleport, Lucky Charm defers the teleport choice first; resolving that choice applies the hidden Atlas draw and then the chosen teleport on the deferred resolve-start-turn-trigger action.

When one minion carries both start-of-controller-turn Spellbook draw and nearby-enemy lure, the Start Phase resolves them in order on a single lure-branch action: draw a spell first, then move the chosen nearby enemy one step closer. The engine still issues lure-target branch actions when a valid target exists.

When the same start-turn draw-plus-lure minion has no nearby enemy, the Start Phase still draws the spell on the simple resolve-start-turn-trigger action and the lure no-ops without moving any minion.

When one site carries both Genesis discard-top-spells and draw-a-spell per adjacent same-card site, playing it resolves adjacent draws first, then publicly discards the top two spells from the controller's Spellbook.
When the same discard-plus-adjacent-draw site has no adjacent same-card site, Genesis still publicly discards the top two spells and does not draw.

A 2x2 minion that may Ranged strike once during basic movement and may step after a Ranged strike can fire from any occupied footprint cell while movement is paused, then take the optional post-strike step that translates every occupied cell before basic movement resumes.

When the same 2x2 minion declines the optional post-strike step after a during-movement Ranged strike, basic movement resumes from the starting footprint and the declared path still completes normally.
When one site carries both Genesis gain mana and optional paid-token summon, declining the token still grants the printed mana after the site is played.
When the same site pays 1 mana for its Genesis token, the controller still receives the printed mana net of the token payment before the token enters play.
When one site carries both Genesis gain-mana and may-bottom-next-spell, playing it publicly gains mana first, then enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may bottom the next spell.
When the same gain-mana and may-bottom site is played, declining the bottom choice keeps the Spellbook order while the mana gain remains resolved.

When one site carries both Genesis gain-mana and reorder-next-spells, playing it publicly gains mana first, then enters hidden spell-order Genesis where the controller may reorder the next three spells.
When the same gain-mana and reorder site is played, choosing the identity order keeps the Spellbook order while the mana gain remains resolved.
When one site carries both Genesis gain-mana and discard-top-spells, playing it publicly gains mana first, then publicly discards the top two spells from the controller's Spellbook.

When the same gain-mana and discard-top-spells site is played with fewer than two spells in the Spellbook, the mana gain still resolves and only the available top spell is publicly discarded without deck-out.

When one site carries both optional paid-token summon and may-bottom-next-spell, paying for the token resolves first, then the controller enters hidden spell Genesis where they may bottom the next spell.
When the same paid-token and may-bottom site is played, declining the token still enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may keep the Spellbook order.
When one site carries both optional paid-token summon and discard-top-spells, declining the token still publicly discards the top two spells from the controller's Spellbook after the site is played.
When the same paid-token and discard-top-spells site is played, the token enters play first, then the top two spells are publicly discarded.

When one site carries both may-bottom-next-spell and reorder-next-spells, playing it enters hidden spell Genesis first, then privately reorders the next three spells after the controller bottoms the top spell.
When the same may-bottom and reorder site is played, keeping the top spell still chains into hidden reorder Genesis where the controller may confirm the unchanged top-three order.

When one site carries both optional paid-token summon and reorder-next-spells, paying for the token resolves first, then the controller enters hidden reorder Genesis where they may privately reorder the next three spells.
When the same paid-token and reorder site is played, declining the token still enters hidden reorder Genesis where the controller may confirm the unchanged top-three order.

When one site carries both discard-top-spells and may-bottom-next-spell, playing it publicly discards the top two spells first, then enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may bottom the new top spell.
When the same discard-top and may-bottom site is played, keeping the new top spell after the two public discards completes Genesis without reordering the remaining spellbook.

When one site carries both discard-top-spells and reorder-next-spells, playing it publicly discards the top two spells first, then enters hidden reorder Genesis where the controller may reorder the next three spells.
When the same discard-top and reorder site is played, confirming the unchanged top-three order after the two public discards completes Genesis without further spellbook changes.

When one site carries both Genesis gain-mana and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, playing it adjacent to a matching site publicly gains mana first, then draws one spell for each bordering matching site.
When the same gain-mana and adjacent-draw site is played without a bordering matching site, only the mana gain resolves and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries both draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card and may-bottom-next-spell, playing it adjacent to a matching site publicly draws for each bordering match first, then enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may bottom the new top spell.
When the same adjacent-draw and may-bottom site is played, keeping the new top spell after the adjacent draws completes Genesis without further spellbook changes.

When one site carries both draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card and reorder-next-spells, playing it adjacent to a matching site publicly draws for each bordering match first, then enters hidden reorder Genesis where the controller may reorder the next three spells.
When the same adjacent-draw and reorder site is played, confirming the unchanged top-three order after the adjacent draws completes Genesis without further spellbook changes.

When one site carries both paid-token and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, playing it adjacent to a matching site and paying one mana summons the token first, then draws one spell for each bordering matching site.
When the same paid-token and adjacent-draw site is played, declining the token still draws one spell for each bordering matching site.

When one site carries both draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card and enemies-lose-stealth, playing it adjacent to a matching site strips enemy Stealth first, then draws one spell for each bordering matching site.
When the same adjacent-draw and stealth-strip site is played with no bordering matching site and no stealthed enemies, only the site-played event resolves and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries both draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card and heal-nearby-avatars, playing it adjacent to a matching site heals nearby avatars first, then draws one spell for each bordering matching site.
When the same adjacent-draw and heal-nearby site is played with no bordering matching site and nearby avatars already at maximum life, only the site-played event resolves and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries both draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card and immobilize-nearby-until-next-turn, playing it adjacent to a matching site creates the immobile area first, then draws one spell for each bordering matching site.
When the same adjacent-draw and immobilize-nearby site is played with no bordering matching site, the immobile area resolves and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries both pay-one-mana-for-token and strip-enemy-stealth Genesis, paying for the token resolves the token first, then strips stealth from adjacent enemies, then draws one spell per bordering matching site.

When the same paid-token and strip-enemy-stealth site is played with the token declined, stealth is stripped from adjacent enemies and one spell is drawn per bordering matching site without summoning a token.
When one site carries both heal-nearby-avatars and may-bottom-next-spell Genesis, playing it heals nearby avatars first, then privately offers bottom-or-keep on the next spell.
When the same heal-nearby and may-bottom-next-spell site resolves, keeping the next spell preserves spellbook order after the heal completes.
When one site carries both immobilize-nearby-until-next-turn and reorder-next-spells Genesis, playing it creates the immobile area first, then privately offers reordering the next three spells.
When the same immobilize-nearby and reorder-next-spells site resolves, keeping spell order preserves the private spellbook order after the immobile area is created.

When one site carries both first-copy-only Genesis gain-mana and discard-top-spells, playing it as the only controlled copy publicly gains the conditional mana first, then publicly discards the top two spells from the controller's Spellbook.
When a site carries first-copy-only Genesis gain-mana, playing a second controlled copy of the same card resolves site play but does not grant the conditional mana again.

When one site carries both first-copy-only Genesis gain-mana and may-bottom-next-spell, playing it as the only controlled copy publicly gains the conditional mana first, then enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may bottom the next spell.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana and may-bottom site is played, declining the bottom choice keeps the Spellbook order while the conditional mana gain remains resolved.

When one site carries both first-copy-only Genesis gain-mana and reorder-next-spells, playing it as the only controlled copy publicly gains the conditional mana first, then enters hidden spell-order Genesis where the controller may reorder the next three spells.

When one site carries both first-copy-only Genesis gain-mana and optional paid-token summon, paying for the token as the only controlled copy still grants the conditional mana net of the token payment.

When one site carries both first-copy-only Genesis gain-mana and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana and adjacent-draw site is played without a bordering matching site, only the conditional mana gain resolves on the first controlled copy and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries both first-copy-only gain-mana, strip-enemy-stealth, and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site strips nearby enemy Stealth and draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.

When the same first-copy-only gain-mana and strip-stealth site is played without a bordering matching site, only the conditional mana gain resolves on the first controlled copy and no Stealth is stripped.

When one site carries both first-copy-only gain-mana, heal-nearby-avatars, and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site heals the nearby Avatar and draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana and heal-nearby site is played without a bordering matching site, only the conditional mana gain resolves on the first controlled copy and no Avatar is healed.

When one site carries both first-copy-only gain-mana, immobilize-nearby-until-next-turn, and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site creates the immobile area and draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.

When the same first-copy-only gain-mana and immobilize-nearby site is played without a bordering matching site, the conditional mana gain and local immobile area both resolve on the first controlled copy and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, optional paid-token summon, and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, paying for the token on a later copy adjacent to a matching site summons the token and draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, paid-token, and adjacent-draw site is played on a later copy, declining the token still draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, and may-bottom-next-spell, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site draws one spell, then enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may bottom the new top spell.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, adjacent-draw, and may-bottom site is played on a later copy, keeping the next spell preserves Spellbook order after the adjacent draw completes.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, and reorder-next-spells, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site draws one spell, then enters hidden spell-order Genesis where the controller may reorder the next three spells.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, adjacent-draw, and reorder site is played on a later copy, choosing the identity order keeps Spellbook order after the adjacent draw completes.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, and discard-top-spells, playing a later copy adjacent to a matching site draws one spell, then publicly discards the top two spells from the controller's Spellbook.

When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, adjacent-draw, and discard-top site is played without a bordering matching site, the conditional mana gain and top-two discards resolve on the first controlled copy and no spell is drawn.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, optional paid-token summon, strip-enemy-stealth, and draw-spell-per-adjacent-same-card, paying for the token on a later copy adjacent to a matching site summons the token, strips nearby enemy Stealth, and draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.

When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, paid-token, strip-stealth, and adjacent-draw site is played on a later copy, declining the token still strips nearby enemy Stealth and draws one spell without granting the conditional mana again.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana and optional paid-token summon alongside strip-enemy-stealth, paying for the token on the first controlled copy grants the conditional mana net of the token payment.
When the same first-copy-only gain-mana and paid-token site is played on the first controlled copy, declining the token still grants the conditional mana gain.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, heal-nearby-avatars, and may-bottom-next-spell, playing the first controlled copy publicly heals the nearby Avatar and gains the conditional mana, then enters hidden spell Genesis where the controller may bottom the next spell.

When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, heal-nearby, and may-bottom site is played on the first controlled copy, keeping the next spell preserves Spellbook order while the heal and conditional mana gain remain resolved.

When one site carries first-copy-only gain-mana, immobilize-nearby-until-next-turn, and reorder-next-spells, playing the first controlled copy creates the immobile area and gains the conditional mana, then enters hidden spell-order Genesis where the controller may reorder the next three spells.

When the same first-copy-only gain-mana, immobilize-nearby, and reorder site is played on the first controlled copy, choosing the identity order keeps Spellbook order while the immobile area and conditional mana gain remain resolved.
When a token minion carries both Stealth and Genesis disable-until-damaged, entering play disables the token and permanently strips its Stealth before any other Genesis resolves.
When a spellbook minion carries both Stealth and Genesis disable-until-damaged, summoning it disables the minion and permanently strips its Stealth on entry.

When a minion carries both optional targeted adjacent Genesis damage and random-card alternative summon payment, the engine offers discard-payment branches with decline and target choices; declining discards one random hand card and summons without Genesis damage.

When a minion carries both optional targeted adjacent Genesis damage and random-card alternative summon payment, choosing a legal adjacent target discards one random hand card, summons the minion, and deals the printed Genesis damage through the shared damage pipeline.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and draw-site Genesis, paid site entry disables the token and then draws one hidden Atlas card.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and draw-site Genesis, summoning it disables the minion and then draws one hidden Atlas card.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and draw-spell Genesis, paid site entry disables the token and then draws one hidden Spellbook card.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and draw-spell Genesis, summoning it disables the minion and then draws one hidden Spellbook card.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and optional adjacent Genesis damage, declining the damage disables the token without dealing damage.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and optional adjacent Genesis damage, choosing a legal target disables the minion and then deals the printed Genesis damage.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and controller-heal Genesis, paid site entry disables the token and then heals its controller through the shared printed-life cap.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and controller-heal Genesis, summoning it disables the minion and then heals its controller through the shared printed-life cap.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and controller-life-loss Genesis, paid site entry disables the token and then makes its controller lose 2 life.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and controller-life-loss Genesis, summoning it disables the minion and then makes its controller lose 2 life.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and strike-each-enemy-here Genesis, paid site entry disables the token and then strikes every enemy sharing its location.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and strike-each-enemy-here Genesis, summoning it disables the minion and then strikes every enemy sharing its location.
When a token minion carries both disable-until-damaged and here-area Genesis damage, paid site entry disables the token and then damages each other unit sharing its site.
When a spellbook minion carries both disable-until-damaged and here-area Genesis damage, summoning it disables the minion and then damages each other unit sharing its site.
When a site carries both unconditional and first-copy-only Genesis mana, playing the first controlled copy grants both amounts.
When a site carries both unconditional and first-copy-only Genesis mana, playing a later controlled copy grants only the unconditional amount.

When a minion carries both optional targeted adjacent Genesis damage and local-minion sacrifice summon payment, the engine offers sacrifice-payment branches with decline and target choices; declining sacrifices one controlled minion at the summoning location and summons without Genesis damage.

When a minion carries both optional targeted adjacent Genesis damage and local-minion sacrifice summon payment, choosing a legal adjacent target sacrifices one controlled minion at the summoning location, summons the minion, and deals the printed Genesis damage through the shared damage pipeline.
When a spellbook minion carries stacked Genesis draw-spell, life loss, and controller heal, summoning it resolves draw, then life loss, then healing through the shared printed-life cap.
When a token minion carries stacked Genesis draw-spell, life loss, and controller heal, paid site entry resolves draw, then life loss, then healing through the shared printed-life cap.
Two distinct synthetic decks played by the baseline policy reach at least one committed fight within a bounded deterministic rollout, and the full transcript replays byte-identically.
Two distinct synthetic decks played by the baseline policy reach a terminal win with at least one fight, and the full transcript replays byte-identically.
The terminal synthetic deck-pair batch runner reproduces the same transcript hash and verified replay across repeated native batch executions.
A finished synthetic demo with verified replay passes every TEST-04 gate and classifies as rules-complete but authority-unverified rather than partial-rules.
A 2x2 Landbound minion stays enabled when Flood covers only part of its footprint, because any remaining occupied land location keeps Landbound satisfied.
A 2x2 Landbound minion becomes Disabled in place when Flood covers every occupied cell of its footprint.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion stays enabled when Drought covers only part of its footprint, because any remaining occupied Water location keeps Waterbound satisfied.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion becomes Disabled in place when Drought covers every occupied cell of its footprint.
A 2x2 Landbound minion is Disabled on an all-Water footprint and becomes enabled in place when Drought covers every occupied cell, because Drought makes those sites land again.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion is Disabled on an all-land footprint and becomes enabled in place when Flood covers every occupied cell, because Flood makes those sites Water.

Magic that gains control of a target enemy minion this turn may choose a distant enemy, transfers control without changing ownership, and untaps that minion so its new controller can use it immediately.
Temporary enemy-minion control expires at the current End Phase and restores the previous controller without changing ownership.
Magic that gains control of a target enemy minion until it loses Stealth may choose a distant enemy, transfers control without changing ownership, grants Stealth, and taps that minion.
Stealth-bound enemy-minion control survives the current End Phase and restores the previous controller when the stolen minion loses Stealth, without changing ownership.

Minion Genesis that gains control of tapped minions here until this leaves steals each tapped minion sharing its footprint without targeting, leaves Ward intact, skips untapped and distant minions, and keeps control through the current End Phase.
Source-bound Genesis control restores the previous controller when the source leaves play, without changing ownership.

A carried Artifact that is sacrificed to steal a target enemy minion here grants its bearer control of that minion until the bearer leaves, offers only unstealthed enemy minions sharing the bearer's footprint, and leaves ownership unchanged.
Sacrifice-to-steal Artifact control survives the current End Phase and restores the previous controller when the bearer leaves play, without changing ownership.

A minion that lets nearby Avatars discard a card to gain control of it offers that paid steal only to a nearby Avatar, transfers control without targeting so Ward does not absorb, and leaves ownership unchanged.
Nearby-Avatar discard control is permanent: it survives End Phase, does not revert when the source stays in play, and is not offered to a distant Avatar.

Genesis that lets the previous player control each player during their next turn schedules that swap immediately, then the previous player submits the opponent's next turn, sees that player's hidden hand, and spends that player's resources while the controlled player cannot act.
Previous-player turn control applies to each player's next turn once, then expires: after both scheduled turns resolve, each player submits their own decisions again.
