Magic that draws a site and then may play a land site draws one hidden Atlas card, then offers an extra play of a printed land site plus a decline. The extra play is legal while the Avatar is already tapped and does not tap the Avatar. Printed water sites are not offered.

Magic that draws a site and then may play a water site offers only printed water sites after the draw. Declining leaves the drawn water site in hand and returns to the main phase without tapping the Avatar.

Magic that disables a minion within two measured steps until damaged offers only same-region minions at the caster's occupied cells or a cardinal walk of at most two steps. Avatars and a minion three steps away are not offered. The chosen minion becomes Disabled until it takes damage, cannot use printed abilities, and wakes after positive damage.

Enemy Ward absorbs measured disable-until-damaged Magic and breaks without applying the disable. A successful disable lasts through the caster's next Start Phase instead of expiring like Freeze, and stays until the minion takes damage.

Magic that grants an allied minion +2 power this turn and then draws a spell offers only allied minions, never an Avatar or an enemy. The power uses the shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. The power expires at End Phase.
Grant-+2-this-turn then draw-spell Magic applies the power first. If the caster's Spellbook is empty, the required draw ends the game as a deck-out without a spell-drawn event.

Magic that grants an allied minion Lethal this turn and then draws a spell offers only allied minions, never an Avatar or an enemy. The Lethal mark uses the shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. Lethal expires at End Phase.
After grant-Lethal-this-turn then draw-spell Magic resolves, one point of damage from that minion destroys a tougher minion. The same strike without the grant only wounds it.

Magic that grants an allied minion Airborne this turn and then draws a spell offers only allied minions, never an Avatar or an enemy. The Airborne mark uses the shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. Airborne expires at End Phase.
A grounded minion cannot strike an Airborne enemy. After grant-Airborne-this-turn then draw-spell Magic resolves, that same minion can strike the Airborne enemy.

Magic that grants an ally +1 movement this turn and then draws a spell offers allied Avatars and minions, never an enemy. The movement mark uses a shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. The movement expires at End Phase.

A minion with no printed movement bonus can reach an adjacent cell but not a cell two steps away. After grant-+1-movement-this-turn then draw-spell Magic resolves, that same minion can reach the two-step cell.
Genesis that untaps adjacent allies untaps a tapped Avatar on a bordering cell in the same region. An enemy minion two steps away is not untapped.
Genesis that untaps adjacent allies does not untap a tapped Avatar sharing the newcomer's cell. Same-cell is not adjacent.
Grant-Stealth-to-allied-minions then draw-spell Magic stealths every allied minion, never the Avatar or an enemy, and then draws one hidden spell.
Grant-Stealth-to-allied-minions then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no allied minion is in play. No minion is stealthed.

Grant-Stealth-to-an-allied-minion occupying an enemy site then draw-spell Magic offers only an allied minion standing on an enemy-controlled site, stealths that minion, and then draws one hidden spell. Allies on friendly sites, Avatars, and enemy minions are not offered.
Grant-Stealth-to-an-allied-minion occupying an enemy site then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no allied minion occupies an enemy site. A home-site ally is not stealthed.
Summon-token-to-allied-minion then draw-spell Magic summons one source-linked token onto an allied minion's surface cell and then draws one hidden spell. Avatars and enemy minions are not hosts.
Summon-token-to-allied-minion then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no allied minion is in play. No token is summoned.
Ward-each-allied-minion-at-target-water-site Magic offers only Water sites, Wards every allied minion occupying the chosen site, and leaves an enemy minion there unwarded.
Ward-each-allied-minion-at-target-water-site Magic does not offer an Earth site. Targeting a Water site with no allied minion is a paid no-op.

Pull-adjacent-aboveground-unit-to-target-water-site then draw-spell Magic offers a Water site and an aboveground unit bordering that site, pulls that unit onto the site, and then draws one hidden spell. A unit occupying the site is not adjacent. Earth sites are not offered.
Pull-adjacent-aboveground-unit-to-target-water-site then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no aboveground unit borders a Water site. No unit is moved.

Return-up-to-three-cemetery-cards-to-deck-bottom then draw-spell Magic offers each subset of up to three own-cemetery cards, returns the chosen cards to the bottoms of their owners' matching decks in instance-id order, and then draws one hidden spell.
Return-up-to-three-cemetery-cards-to-deck-bottom then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no cemetery card is returned. The just-cast Magic stays in the cemetery.

Ward-nearby-minion-or-site Magic offers each nearby minion and each nearby site, including an enemy minion on the caster's cell. A far site is not offered. Choosing a minion applies the shared Ward mark.
Ward-nearby-minion-or-site Magic can Ward a nearby site. The next targeted destroy consumes that one-shot mark, leaves the site in play, and then a second destroy removes it.

Silence-and-tap-nearby-minion then may-draw-spell Magic offers each nearby minion with or without a spell draw. Choosing the draw Silences and taps that minion, then draws one hidden spell. A far minion is not offered. Silence is this-turn ability loss, not Disable, so a printed Spellcaster cannot cast while Silenced while the Avatar still can.
Silence-and-tap-nearby-minion then may-draw-spell Magic still Silences and taps when the spell draw is declined. Silence expires at End Phase; the tap remains.

Ally-submerges-target-nearby-minion Magic offers each controlled ally paired with each other minion nearby that ally, including an enemy on the ally's cell. A far minion is not offered. Choosing an ally and a nearby minion on a Water site submerges that minion.
Ally-submerges-target-nearby-minion Magic still offers a nearby pair on an Earth site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underwater layer exists.

Ally-strikes-each-enemy-at-its-location Magic offers each controlled ally and makes that ally strike every enemy sharing its current cell and region. A far enemy is not struck. The ally does not step.
Ally-strikes-each-enemy-at-its-location Magic still offers each controlled ally when no enemy shares that location, then resolves as a paid no-op without a strike.

Burrow-target-adjacent-minion Magic offers only a minion that borders the caster. A same-cell minion and a far minion are not offered. Choosing an adjacent minion on an Earth site burrows that minion.
Burrow-target-adjacent-minion Magic still offers an adjacent minion on a Water site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists.

Ally-takes-up-to-two-steps Magic offers each controlled ally paired with each card-effect destination within two cardinal steps. After C4, C3, and C2 exist, an ally at C4 is offered C2, C3, and C4, not C1. Casting to C2 emits a two-step unit-stepped event.
Ally-takes-up-to-two-steps Magic still offers the ally's current cell. Choosing to stay resolves as a paid no-op without a unit-stepped event.

Teleport-target-minion-artifact-or-aura-one-diagonal Magic offers a minion paired with an existing diagonal location. After C4, D4, and D3 exist, a minion at C4 is offered D3 only. Casting teleports that minion to D3 without a step.
Teleport-target-minion-artifact-or-aura-one-diagonal Magic offers no cast when the only extra site is cardinal. A minion at C4 with C3 present cannot be teleported.

Grant-double-damage-to-ally-next-strike-this-turn Magic marks a chosen ally. That ally's next unit strike this turn deals double damage, so an attack-2 minion kills a defense-3 enemy that it would only wound without the grant.
The next-strike-double mark expires at End Phase. A later strike uses the ally's printed attack and only wounds the same tougher enemy.

Kill-mortal-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic offers the same measured locations as area damage: existing sites within two cardinal steps of the caster footprint. Casting at a shared site kills every Mortal minion there, leaves a non-Mortal occupant unwounded, and does not kill a Mortal three cardinal steps away.

Kill-mortal-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location that holds only a non-Mortal minion. Casting there is a paid no-op: the non-Mortal stays unwounded and the spell still resolves.

Destroy-artifacts-and-auras-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic offers locations within two measured steps of the caster. After C4 and C3 exist, choosing C3 destroys a loose Artifact there and leaves a far Artifact at C1, which is three steps away and not offered.
Destroy-artifacts-and-auras-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location with no Artifact or Aura. Choosing that location resolves as a paid no-op.

Destroy-minions-at-water-site-within-two-steps Magic offers only Water sites within two measured cardinal steps of the caster footprint. Casting at C4 kills every minion occupying that Water site, including a non-Mortal, and leaves a Mortal three cardinal steps away at C1. An Earth site at C3 is not offered.
Destroy-minions-at-water-site-within-two-steps Magic still offers an empty Water site. Casting there is a paid no-op: the spell still resolves.

Banish-demon-and-undead-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic offers the same measured locations as Mortality: existing sites within two cardinal steps of the caster footprint. Casting at a shared site banishes every Demon or Undead minion there, leaves a living non-Demon non-Undead occupant untouched, and does not offer or banish an Undead three cardinal steps away.

Banish-demon-and-undead-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location that holds only a non-Demon non-Undead minion. Casting there is a paid no-op: the occupant stays and the spell still resolves.

Destroy-undead-minions-and-artifacts-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic offers locations within two measured steps of the caster. After C4 and C3 exist, choosing C3 kills an Undead minion and destroys a loose Artifact there, and leaves a non-Undead beast at C4 unwounded.
Destroy-undead-minions-and-artifacts-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location with no Undead minion or Artifact. Choosing that location resolves as a paid no-op.

Destroy-own-artifact-at-location-for-area-damage Magic offers a controlled loose or carried Artifact paired with its location. After a relic sits at C3 with an enemy minion there, casting destroys that relic and deals 3 damage to each other Unit at C3.
Destroy-own-artifact-at-location-for-area-damage Magic is unoffered when the caster controls no Artifact, even if an enemy Artifact is in play.

Summon-token-to-each-controlled-site-bordering-enemy-site Magic places one source-linked token on every controlled site that borders an enemy-controlled site, in stable cell order. After North controls C4, C3, C1 and South controls B2 with a minion there, casting summons foot-soldier tokens onto B3 and C3.

Summon-token-to-each-controlled-site-bordering-enemy-site Magic still resolves when no controlled site borders an enemy site. Casting with only C4 in play is a paid no-op: no tokens appear and the spell still resolves.

Disable-target-nearby-minion-until-next-turn Magic offers a minion within nearby range of the caster footprint. Casting disables that minion until the caster's next Start Phase, blocking its actions while disabled, then the flag expires on that boundary.
Disable-target-nearby-minion-until-next-turn Magic does not offer a minion three measured cardinal steps away from the caster footprint, even when a closer minion is legal.

Summon-random-minion-from-any-cemetery Magic selects one random minion from either cemetery, then offers free placement onto a legal site. After a minion dies to the cemetery, casting Raise Dead returns that minion to C4 at zero mana.
Summon-random-minion-from-any-cemetery Magic still resolves when both cemeteries hold no minions. Casting with empty cemeteries is a paid no-op: magic-cast and magic-resolved only.
Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic burrows a chosen minion on an Earth site. After a Burrowing minion occupies C1, casting moves that minion underground and it stays in play.
Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic still offers a minion on a Water site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists. The minion stays on the surface unchanged.

Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic burrows every surface minion at the chosen land site in canonical instance-id order. After two Burrowing minions occupy C1, casting at that site moves both underground and they stay in play.
Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic does not offer a water-only site, because no Underground layer exists there. An Earth site remains offered.

Damage-each-unit-at-location-within-two-steps Magic offers existing locations within two measured cardinal steps of the caster footprint. After C4 and C3 exist, choosing C3 deals 3 damage to each Unit there: an unwarded minion takes 3, Ward absorbs for a second minion, and Avatars at C4 and C1 stay unwounded. Location offers are not unit targets, so Stealth does not filter them.
Damage-each-unit-at-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers an empty measured location. Casting at empty C3 is a paid no-op: magic-cast and magic-resolved only.

Submerge-target-minion Magic offers a same-region minion at a Water site and forcefully submerges a Submerge minion there. After south summons at C1 on a Water site, casting Drown moves the minion underwater and keeps it in play.
Submerge-target-minion Magic at an earth-only site resolves as a paid no-op because no underwater layer exists there.
Return-minion-from-own-cemetery Magic offers only the caster's own cemetery minions and returns the chosen instance to the hidden Spellbook hand with source-linked evidence.
Return-minion-from-own-cemetery Magic with an empty own cemetery still resolves as a paid no-op.
Damage-target-unit Magic offers same-region minions and deals lethal damage through the shared death pipeline when defense is exceeded.
Damage-target-unit Magic lets enemy Ward absorb the complete damage event and break without dealing damage.
Grant-charge-to-ally-this-turn Magic offers controlled allies, grants temporary Charge, and lets a newly summoned sick minion Move and Attack immediately.
Grant-charge-to-ally-this-turn Magic still offers the caster's Avatar when no allied minion is in play and grants Charge through resolution.
Leap-attack-ally Magic optionally steps a controlled ally before striking every enemy at the destination cell.
Leap-attack-ally Magic lets an immobile ally only stay and strike at its current location without stepping.
Lure-enemy-minion-one-step-closer Magic tempts a nearby enemy minion to take its own closer step toward the caster's ally.
Lure-enemy-minion-one-step-closer Magic still resolves as a paid no-op when no nearby enemy minion qualifies.
Fight-ally-with-adjacent-enemy Magic makes a chosen ally fight a targeted adjacent enemy through the shared fight pipeline.
Fight-ally-with-adjacent-enemy Magic breaks Ward on the target without entering combat.
Damage-each-aboveground-minion Magic simultaneously damages every aboveground minion.
Damage-each-aboveground-minion Magic lets Ward absorb the damage on a surviving minion.
Damage-random-unit-at-location Magic targets a surface location and deterministically damages one random unit there.
Damage-random-unit-at-location Magic lets Ward absorb the random hit without dealing damage.
Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic kills only a wounded minion in the caster region.
Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic offers no target when every minion in the caster region is healthy.
Tap-target-minion Magic exhausts a ready same-region minion.
Tap-target-minion Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and no tap event is emitted.
Untap-target-minion Magic readies a tapped same-region minion without breaking Ward.
Untap-target-minion Magic that targets an already-untapped minion is a paid no-op.
Grant-Ward Magic marks an unwarded same-region minion without breaking an existing mark.
Grant-Ward Magic that targets an already-warded minion is a paid no-op.
Grant-Stealth Magic hides an enemy minion from later targeting.
Grant-Stealth Magic does not offer an already-stealthed enemy minion.
Kill-target-minion Magic destroys a healthy same-region minion and never offers an Avatar.
Kill-target-minion Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and the minion survives.
Bounce Magic returns a healthy same-region minion to its owner's hand and never offers an Avatar.
Bounce Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and the minion stays on the board.

Destroy-site Magic offers every real site including the caster's own, never offers Rubble or a void, replaces the chosen site with Rubble, and moves that site into its owner's cemetery. Occupants remain on the Rubble.
Destroy-site Magic that would destroy a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site in play, and still resolves.
Return-site Magic returns a real site to its owner's Atlas hand, leaves no Rubble, and banishes surface minions occupying it. Avatars remain at the emptied cell.
Return-site Magic that would return a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site and its occupants in play, and still resolves.

Mill-spell Magic offers only both Avatars, never a minion, and puts the printed number of the chosen player's top Spellbook cards into that owner's cemetery in deck order. Identities are public. The game stays active when cards remain.
Mill-spell Magic that finds an empty Spellbook is a paid no-op. It does not draw, does not lose to deck-out, and emits no discard events.
Mill-site Magic is the Atlas sibling of mill-spell Magic: it offers only both Avatars and puts top Atlas cards into the owner's cemetery in deck order without drawing or decking.
Mill-site Magic that finds an empty Atlas is a paid no-op. It does not draw, does not lose to deck-out, and emits no discard events.
Return-artifact Magic detaches a carried Artifact and returns it to its owner's Spellbook hand. The opponent sees only the resulting hand count, and the Artifact does not enter a cemetery.
Return-artifact Magic offers no target when no Artifact occupies the caster region, including when only a minion is in play.

Destroy-artifact Magic offers every Artifact in the caster region whether loose or carried, moves a real Artifact into its owner's cemetery, and leaves no later Artifact target once the realm is empty of them.
Destroy-artifact Magic offers no target when no Artifact occupies the caster region, including when only a minion is in play.

Cemetery Magic return is the Rescue sibling for Magic cards: it offers only Magic in the caster's own cemetery, never a minion, site, artifact, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.
Cemetery Magic return that finds no Magic in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Artifact return is the Rescue sibling for Artifacts: it offers only Artifacts in the caster's own cemetery, never a Magic card, minion, site, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.

Cemetery Artifact return that finds no Artifact in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Site return is the Rescue sibling for Sites: it offers only Sites in the caster's own cemetery, never Magic already there, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Atlas hand rather than the Spellbook.

Cemetery Site return that finds no Site in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Aura return is the Rescue sibling for Auras: it offers only Auras in the caster's own cemetery, never a Magic card, minion, site, artifact, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.

Cemetery Aura return that finds no Aura in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Target-player discard Magic offers only both Avatars. After the cast is announced, the targeted player chooses one of their own Atlas or Spellbook hand cards. The choice is a pending Storyline that transfers the decision seat; the caster cannot pick the card, and opponent hand identities stay redacted until the discard is public in the cemetery.
The same targeted discard is a paid no-op when the chosen player has no hand cards. It never becomes a random discard and never decks out.
Targetless draw-spell Magic pays its cost, draws the printed number of hidden Spellbook cards in deck order, and enters its owner's cemetery. The opponent sees only the new hand count.
Targetless draw-spell Magic draws every remaining Spellbook card it can, then loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library.
Targetless draw-site Magic pays its cost, draws the printed number of hidden Atlas cards in deck order, and enters its owner's cemetery. The opponent sees only the new Atlas hand count.
Targetless draw-site Magic draws every remaining Atlas card it can, then loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library.
Target-player life-loss Magic pays its cost, offers only both Avatars, never offers a minion, and reduces the chosen Avatar's life without dealing damage. The loss is not a death blow.
Target-player life-loss Magic that reduces an Avatar to zero life reaches Death's Door without ending the game. Further life loss against that Avatar is a no-op and is never a death blow.

Target-player life-gain Magic pays its cost, offers only both Avatars, never offers a minion, and heals the chosen Avatar through the shared printed-life cap. Unlike controller-only healing, it can restore an opponent.
Target-player life-gain Magic that would heal an Avatar at Death's Door is a paid no-op. Life stays at zero, the game stays active, and no healing event is emitted.

A player-chosen additional discard cost is a Storyline choice among every other hand card. It cannot select the spell being cast, pays into the owner's cemetery before the cast is announced, and then the companion effect resolves.

The same additional discard cost issues no cast when the caster has no other hand card. Remaining copies of the spell still count as other hand cards; an empty Atlas and a singleton Spellbook leave the spell unoffered.

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic burrows a chosen ordinary minion on an Earth site. The minion has no Burrowing, so region settlement kills it immediately after the burrow and it goes to its owner's cemetery.
Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic still offers an ordinary minion on a Water site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists. The minion stays on the surface unchanged.

Craterize-style Magic pays an Atlas discard, destroys an unprotected site into Rubble, and deals its printed grid damage to the occupant. Plain destroy-site Magic (0623) creates Rubble without dealing damage.

Craterize-style Magic that would destroy a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site in play, still pays the Atlas discard, still deals its grid damage to the occupant, and still resolves. Plain destroy-site protection (0624) has no damage companion.

Nearby-control Magic transfers a minion and its Deathrite to the new controller. Targeted Magic is a non-unit source: killing the stolen minion draws a site for the thief, and the corpse still enters the owner's cemetery.
Nearby-control Magic does not offer a far minion. Targeted Magic still kills that minion as a non-unit source and resolves Deathrite for the original controller.

Freeze Magic that disables a nearby minion until the caster's next Start Phase offers a same-region minion occupying the caster footprint. Casting disables that minion, blocking its actions until the flag expires on that turn boundary.
Freeze Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and the minion is not Disabled.
Heal-target-minion Magic removes damage from a living minion in the same turn it was wounded. Avatars are not legal targets. The heal does not kill the minion.
Heal-target-minion Magic offers only minions. A Death's Door Avatar is never a legal target. Healing an undamaged minion is a paid no-op: no heal event is emitted and the minion stays at zero damage.
Magic can grant Airborne to a controlled ally for the current turn. The grant is recorded on minions as a temporary source, and public observations show the minion as Airborne.
Grant-Airborne Magic still records a temporary source on a minion that is already Airborne. Shared End Phase cleanup expires that source, and printed Airborne remains.

Destroy-aura Magic offers every realm Aura, moves a real Aura into its owner's cemetery, and leaves no later Aura target once the realm is empty of them. The event is aura-destroyed rather than a return to hand or a duration dispel.
Destroy-aura Magic offers no target when no Aura occupies the realm, including when only a minion is in play.

Return-target-aura Magic returns a realm Flood to its owner's Spellbook hand. The Aura leaves the realm, Flood water leaves the covered sites, the opponent sees only the updated hand count, and the targeting key is the realm Aura rather than a cemetery card.
Return-target-aura Magic offers no target when no Aura occupies the realm, including when only a minion is in play. A minion is not a realm Aura, so the bounce spell stays in hand.

Genesis strike-each-enemy-here hits every enemy sharing the newcomer's cell, including the Avatar standing on its own site. Co-located allies and the striker are skipped. Ward absorbs a strike without dealing damage.

Genesis strike-each-enemy-here does not strike co-located allies or the striker, and it does not reach enemies occupying a different cell. Summoning onto the controller's own site emits no strike when every enemy is elsewhere.
